Thanks for the context, Aisha — quick Deal Desk read below. Attaching a short risk summary (DealDesk_Risk_Summary.xlsx).

Summary assessment:
- Discount: AE-authorized discount cap is 12% for pilot deals of this size. Anything above that requires Director-level signoff.
- MFN / benchmark clause: high risk. We should not agree to a broad MFN that covers private/partner deals or that would tie our pricing for other customers. An MFN limited to "publicly advertised list prices for hosted API inference units" and restricted to the exact metric used in the SOW (inference units per model per region) is defensible. Timebox: 12 months.
- Exclusivity: a full exclusivity grant is higher risk than the commercial benefit warrants for a pilot. If we consider it, it must be model-specific, limited to the clinical model in the SOW, and include a performance/usage floor (if BrightPath doesn't reach X inference units in month 3, exclusivity lapses).
- Comms/legal: any MFN must include carveouts for: (a) partner/channel deals (b) pilot/PO-level promotional credits (c) enterprise committed-capacity pricing.

Proposed counter-offer (Deal Desk recommendation):
- Pilot discount: 12% (compromise between 10% and their 15%)
- MFN: counter with a "price-parity on posted public API rates" clause, 12-month term, scoped to the model and NA region only, explicitly carved out from partner/channel programs and pre-negotiated enterprise reserved capacity contracts.
- Exclusivity: deny a standalone exclusivity grant; offer a conditional limited model-specific exclusivity that requires execution of a conversion SOW and a 6-month usage floor (we can propose X=250k inference units).
- Approvals required: any deviation (discount >12% or open-ended MFN/exclusivity) needs VP Sales + GC signoff.

Next steps:
1) Rishi — can you draft a short redline for the MFN/benchmark language that implements the carveouts above?
2) Aisha — if they push on 15% or broad MFN, escalate to VP Sales; provide a rundown of the strategic levers (referral, pipeline influence) they can offer in return.

Attachments: DealDesk_Risk_Summary.xlsx

- Marissa

Aisha / Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the Deal Desk analysis. I reviewed the suggested guardrails. Legal is willing to approve a conditional, narrowly scoped concession with the following controls:

1) Discount: approve up to 12% for the pilot (Aisha — you may offer 12%). Any additional discount requires VP Sales approval.

2) MFN / Benchmark language: Legal will NOT accept a broad MFN that covers private deals, partners, or reserved-capacity commitments. We can offer: 
   - A limited "public price parity" clause: Redwood will confirm that, during the 12-month MFN window, BrightPath will be entitled to the same publicly posted list price for the same model and region, provided BrightPath is purchasing on the same service tier (hosted inference, same token accounting).
   - Explicit carveouts: partner/channel agreements, reserved/dedicated capacity contracts, and case-by-case promotional credits.
   - Clause will include an audit right limited to verifying published prices (no access to Redwood invoices or confidential customer terms).

3) Exclusivity: we decline a unilateral exclusivity grant. We will offer a conditional model-specific exclusivity linked to conversion: if BrightPath signs a conversion SOW within 6 months and meets a minimum usage floor of 250k inference units/month for three consecutive months, Redwood will consider a 6-month model-specific exclusivity limited to NA and bounded by the same carveouts. This must be in a separate conversion SOW with defined termination triggers.

4) Termination/Performance triggers: the pilot SOW must include acceptance criteria and a performance SLA; failure to meet those metrics voids any MFN/exclusivity benefits.

5) Exec approvals: Legal and Deal Desk can sign off on the above. If BrightPath insists on 15% or any form of enterprise-wide MFN or open exclusivity, escalate to VP Sales and GC (I will join the thread).

Aisha — please present the counter-offer to BrightPath as: 12% pilot discount + limited public-price MFN (12 months) + no immediate exclusivity; conditional exclusivity tied to conversion and usage. Include the carveouts and audit limits above. Also include the HubSpot link to the opportunity and attach a redlined SOW for them to review.
